emptyState: This room is empty. Sign in with email to say what still plays. Guest can browse only.

trends.headline: Cross Road Blues
trends.snippet: The 1936 sides still sit in the room. Robert Johnson guitar between the verses, not a myth about a deal.

trends.headline: Are You Experienced
trends.snippet: The inverted Strat. Feedback as composition. Hendrix made the guitar a second voice.

trends.headline: Back to Black
trends.snippet: Ronettes in the arrangement, London in the vowel. Amy Winehouse wrote a record that still walks in.

trends.headline: Without You
trends.snippet: Pete Ham melody, Badfinger chorus that opens like a window. The song keeps doing the work.

trends.headline: Crowns and text as paint
trends.snippet: Jean-Michel Basquiat: crowns, lists, oilstick. The canvas is still talking.

trends.headline: The Soldier
trends.snippet: Rupert Brooke sonnet. Some corner of a foreign field. The poem still stands.

trends.headline: History Lesson — Part II
trends.snippet: D. Boon guitar as a sentence. Minutemen double-time that still swings. Our band could be your life.

trends.headline: Replay
trends.snippet: Kim Jong-hyun writing for SHINee. Falsetto that holds a whole room. The song is the conversation.

places.title: Cross Road Blues
places.snippet: Robert Johnson, 1936. The guitar answers itself. Delta blues that still teaches the room.

places.title: Are You Experienced
places.snippet: Jimi Hendrix. Electric guitar as weather. The Strat flipped; the mix still startles.

places.title: Piece of My Heart
places.snippet: Janis Joplin voice. Texas grain, Big Brother lift. The take still holds.

places.title: The End / Light My Fire
places.snippet: The Doors. Jim Morrison as singer and poet. A long form that is still a performance.

places.title: Turn On Your Love Light
places.snippet: Ron Pigpen McKernan with the Grateful Dead. Organ, blues shout, the band as a room.

places.title: On the Road Again
places.snippet: Alan Blind Owl Wilson, Canned Heat. Harmonica that sits in front of the beat.

places.title: Without You
places.snippet: Pete Ham, Badfinger. A chorus that other singers borrowed because the melody already knew.

places.title: I Am the Cosmos / Thirteen
places.snippet: Chris Bell, Big Star. Power pop with a private sky. Memphis still in the guitar.

places.title: History Lesson — Part II
places.snippet: D. Boon, Minutemen. Punk that talks. Guitar as a complete sentence.

places.title: Crowns (untitled)
places.snippet: Jean-Michel Basquiat paintings. Text, anatomy, a crown in the corner. On the wall, not in a myth.

places.title: Nevermind / Lithium
places.snippet: Kurt Cobain, Nirvana. Quiet-loud as architecture. The tape still has air in it.

places.title: Live Through This (bass)
places.snippet: Kristen Pfaff, Hole. The low end that holds the songs upright.

places.title: Back to Black
places.snippet: Amy Winehouse. Strings, backbeat, a voice that writes its own room.

places.title: The Soldier
places.snippet: Rupert Brooke. The 1914 sonnet. If I should die, think only this of me. The line is the work.

places.title: Star Trek / Like Crazy
places.snippet: Anton Yelchin as Chekov, and the indie close-up. The take is still on the reel.

places.title: Tenement Yard
places.snippet: Jacob Miller, Inner Circle. Reggae that walks. Kingston in the phrasing.

places.title: Replay / SHINee
places.snippet: Kim Jong-hyun. Writing, falsetto, a pop song that still arrives like a letter.
